rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is to tell both sides that each awaits how events turn and which side wins; at the Resurrection they will know who follows the straight path, the Muslims or their opponents.
rows.anchor: منتظر دوائر الزمان، ولمن يكون النصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountain passes are traversable routes so people can find their way.
rows.anchor: فجاجا سبلا } طرقا مسلوكة حتى يهتدوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God protected the sky with stars against devils.
rows.anchor: سقفا محفوظا } بالنجوم من الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's signs here are its sun, moon, and stars; people turn away from them without reflecting.
rows.anchor: شمسها وقمرها ونجومها { معرضون } لا يتفكرون فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The celestial bodies run and travel; a falak is the orbit of the stars.
rows.anchor: يجرون ويسيرون، والفلك: مدار النجوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuld means enduring life; no human before Muhammad was granted everlasting life, and his opponents will not live forever after his death.
rows.anchor: الخلد } دوام البقاء { أفإين مت فهم الخالدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that no human before Muhammad received everlasting life was revealed when his opponents said they awaited fate to overtake him.
rows.anchor:
قالوا:
نتربص به ريب المنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adversity means affliction and poverty, while good means wealth and health; both test whether people show gratitude and patience.
rows.anchor: نختبركم { بالشر } بالبلايا والفقر { والخير } المال والصحة { فتنة } ابتلاء لننظر كيف شكركم وصبركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nun, the man of the fish, is Jonah.
rows.anchor: اذكر صاحب الحوت، وهو يونس عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah left his people angry with them before God had commanded him to leave.
rows.anchor: من بين قومه { مغاضبا } لهم قبل أمرنا له بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah thought God would not decree for him the confinement in the fish's belly that God had decreed.
rows.anchor: أن لن نقضي عليه ما قضينا من حبسه في بطن الحوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three darknesses were the fish's belly, the sea, and the night.
rows.anchor: ظلمة بطن الحوت، وظلمة البحر، وظلمة الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah confessed wrongdoing because he had been angry with his people and left them before receiving permission.
rows.anchor: حيث غاضبت قومي وخرجت من بينهم قبل الإذن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As God rescued Jonah, He rescues believers from distress when they call for His help and supplicate to Him.
rows.anchor: وكما نجيناه { ننجي المؤمنين } من كربهم إذا استغاثوا بنا ودعونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah's plea not to be left alone means he had no child or descendant.
rows.anchor: أي: وحيدا لا ولد لي ولا عقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the best heir because He remains after those who die.
rows.anchor: خير من يبقى بعد من يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points back to the matter just described.
rows.anchor: أي: الأمر ذلك الذي ذكرت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's sacred ordinances are His obligations and established practices.
rows.anchor: فرائض الله وسننه. { وأحلت لكم الأنعام } أن تأكلوها

words: وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ ٱلْأَنْعَٰمُ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَىٰ عَلَيْكُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock may be eaten except for the animals prohibited in the cited passage, including carrion; the exception does not restore pre-Islamic bans such as bahira and saiba.
rows.anchor: معنى هذا النهي تحريم ما حرمه أهل الجاهلية من البحيرة والسائبة وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding the impurity of idols means avoiding their worship.
rows.anchor: يعني: عبادتها { واجتنبوا قول الزور } يعني: الشرك بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The false utterance to be avoided is associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: يعني: الشرك بالله. { حنفاء لله } مسلمين عادلين عن كل دين سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sincere monotheists are Muslims who turn away from every religion besides Islam.
rows.anchor: مسلمين عادلين عن كل دين سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolater is like someone falling from the sky, seized by birds or carried by wind to a remote place: he has perished and strayed far from truth.
rows.anchor: سقط { من السماء } فاختطفته الطير من الهواء، أو ألقته الريح في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honoring God's ritual signs includes fattening sacrificial camels, and is a sign of piety.
rows.anchor: يستسمن البدن { فإن ذلك من } علامات التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers have prospered: they attain happiness and lasting life in Paradise.
rows.anchor: سعد المصدقون، ونالوا البقاء في الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their humility in prayer means being still and keeping their eyes lowered to the place of prostration.
rows.anchor: ساكنون لا يرفعون ابصارهم عن مواضع سجودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They avoid every word and deed that religious law regards as unbecoming.
rows.anchor: عن كل ما لا يجمل في الشرع من قول وفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being active in zakat means paying the obligatory alms.
rows.anchor: للصدقة الواجبة مؤدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They guard their sexual organs against sinful conduct.
rows.anchor: يحفظونها عن المعاصي

words: إِلَّا عَلَىٰٓ أَزْوَٰجِهِمْ أَوْ مَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَٰنُهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercourse with one's wives or enslaved women is excepted, and carries no blame.
rows.anchor: من الإماء { فإنهم غير ملومين } لا يلامون في وطئهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking sexual relations beyond a wife or enslaved woman crosses from lawful conduct into the forbidden.
rows.anchor: المتعدون عن الحلال إلى الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account of the revelation to Noah and the rest of this story is explained in the commentary on Surat Hud.
rows.anchor: الآية. مفسرة في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means to enter the ship; the rest is explained in Surat Hud.
rows.anchor: أي: ادخل في السفينة، والباقي مفسر في سورة هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah asks God for a blessed disembarkation, and God answers by telling him to descend in peace and blessings.
rows.anchor:
فاستجاب الله تعالى دعاءه حيث قال:
اهبط بسلام منا وبركات عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After they came down from the ship, God blessed them; all later people descend from Noah and those who were with him.
rows.anchor: وبارك فيهم بعد إنزالهم من السفينة، حتى كان جميع الخلق من نسل نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The events recounted are signs pointing to God's power.
rows.anchor: لآيات } لدلالات على قدرتنا { وإن كنا لمبتلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God tested their obedience by sending Noah to them.
rows.anchor: مختبرين طاعتهم بإرسال نوح إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later generation God brought into being was the people of ʿAd.
rows.anchor: أحدثنا { قرنا آخرين } يعني: عادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger sent to that people was Hud.
rows.anchor: فأرسلنا فيهم رسولا منهم } وهو هود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the affluent leaders comfortable and gave them abundant means.
rows.anchor: وأترفناهم } أي: نعمناهم ووسعنا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being brought out means being raised alive from the graves.
rows.anchor: مخرجون } أي: من قبوركم أحياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated exclamation means that the promised resurrection is far off or impossible, in the speakers' view.
rows.anchor: هيهات هيهات } بعدا { لما توعدون } من البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean only the near, present life in this world.
rows.anchor: يعني: الحياة الدانية في هذه الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They describe generations replacing one another: the fathers die and the children live.
rows.anchor: نموت ونحيا } يموت الآباء، ويحيا الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophet asks God to help him against his people because they denied him.
rows.anchor: عليهم { بما كذبون } بتكذيبهم إياي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Soon they will regret their denial when punishment comes upon them.
rows.anchor: عن قريب { ليصبحن نادمين } يندمون إذا نزل بهم العذاب على التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's commanded cry of punishment killed them, leaving them still like flood-borne debris, including decayed tree matter.
rows.anchor: صيحة العذاب { بالحق } بالأمر من الله تعالى { فجعلناهم غثاء } هلكى هامدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Perdition” means destruction, and the wrongdoers here are the polytheists.
rows.anchor: فهلاكا { للقوم الظالمين } المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Truth is the Qur'an, which calls to good, while their desires call to evil; if revelation matched their wishes, it would call to polytheism and the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted.
rows.anchor: القرآن الذي يدعو إلى المحاسن { أهواءهم } التي تدعو إلى المقابح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth are signs of God's oneness; a Qur'an tailored to their wishes would promote polytheism and undermine those proofs, as its followers would associate partners with God.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنها خلقت دلالة على توحيد الله، فلو كان القرآن على مرادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder brought to them is their honor in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: بشرفهم في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad is asked whether he seeks a fee or payment from them; God's gift and reward are better.
rows.anchor: جعلا وأجرا { فخراج ربك } فعطاء ربك وثوابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indecency is fornication; hypocrites spread the slander and sought to disgrace believers and increase fornication among them.
rows.anchor: يفشو الزنا { في الذين آمنوا لهم عذاب أليم } وهم المنافقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without God's favor and mercy, He would have hastened the punishment they deserved.
rows.anchor: لعجل لكم الذي تستحقونه من العقوبة

words: مَا زَكَىٰ مِنكُم مِّنْ أَحَدٍ أَبَدًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: None of those who became involved in the slander would have been purified of that sin without God's favor and mercy; He purifies whom He wills through forgiveness.
rows.anchor: ما صلح وطهر من هذا الذنب أحد { منكم } يعني: من الذين خاضوا فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition means that people of virtue and means should not swear to withhold charity; it refers to Abu Bakr.
rows.anchor: ولا يأتل } ولا يحلف { أولو الفضل منكم والسعة } يعني أبا بكر الصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended recipient was Mistah, a poor emigrant and Abu Bakr's maternal cousin, whom Abu Bakr had vowed not to support.
rows.anchor: يعني: مسطحا، وكان مسكينا مهاجرا وكان ابن خالة أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Mistah joined the talk about Aisha, the verse urged Abu Bakr to pardon him; Abu Bakr said he wanted God's forgiveness and resumed the allowance he had provided.
rows.anchor: عنهم لخوضهم في حديث عائشة { ألا تحبون أن يغفر الله لكم } فلما نزلت هذه الآية قال أبو بكر الصديق: بلى، أنا أحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lamp mentioned in the preceding verse is lit in houses, meaning mosques.
rows.anchor: أي: المصباح يوقد في بيوت، يعني: المساجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God authorized the mosques to be built.
rows.anchor: أذن الله أن ترفع } تبنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearts on Judgment Day shift between hope of salvation and fear of destruction.
rows.anchor: بين الطمع في النجاة، والحذر من الهلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People's eyes search in uncertainty about where they will be taken and from which side their book of deeds will arrive.
rows.anchor: بين الطمع في النجاة، والحذر من الهلاك { والأبصار } تتقلب في أي ناحية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rewards them according to the best of their deeds and adds from His bounty what their deeds did not earn.
rows.anchor: بأحسن { ما عملوا ويزيدهم من فضله } ما لم يستحقوه بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers' deeds resemble a mirage seen as water in a hot desert: the thirsty person reaches it and finds nothing, just as the unbeliever finds his deeds useless at death.
rows.anchor: وهو ما يرى في الفلوات عند شدة الحر، كأنه ماء { بقيعة } جمع قاع، وهو المنبسط من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qīʿa is the plural of qāʿ, an expanse of flat ground.
rows.anchor: بقيعة } جمع قاع، وهو المنبسط من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At that point the unbeliever finds God lying in wait and receives the full recompense for his deeds.
rows.anchor: ووجد الله بالمرصاد عند ذلك { فوفاه حسابه } تحمل جزاء عمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabāraka means that God is firmly established and enduring.
rows.anchor: ثبت ودام { الذي نزل الفرقان } القرآن الذي فرق بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Furqan is the Qur'an, which distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: القرآن الذي فرق بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant to whom the Qur'an was sent is Muhammad.
rows.anchor: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { ليكون للعالمين } الجن والإنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worlds warned by the Qur'an are jinn and humans, warned of punishment.
rows.anchor: للعالمين } الجن والإنس { نذيرا } مخوفا من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created everything that can be described as created and assigned it its measure.
rows.anchor: مما يطلق في صفة المخلوق { فقدره تقديرا } جعله على مقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nushūr means life after death.
rows.anchor: نشورا } أي: حياة بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers alleged that the Qur'an was a lie Muhammad invented and that other people, whom they meant to be Jews, helped him; the author calls the accusation false and unjust.
rows.anchor: يعنون: اليهود { فقد جآءو } بهذا القول { ظلما وزورا } كذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They alleged the Qur'an was ancient stories written down and dictated to Muhammad morning and evening by someone teaching him.
rows.anchor: كتبها { فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا } يعنون أنه يختلف إلى من يعلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad should answer that the Qur'an was sent by the One who knows what is hidden in the heavens and earth, and sent it in accordance with His knowledge.
rows.anchor: أنزل القرآن { الذي يعلم السر في السموات والأرض } يعلم بواطن الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer who bites his hands is ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, who had believed and then apostatized to please Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: الكافر، يعني: عقبة بن أبي معيط كان قد آمن ثم ارتد لرضى أبي بن خلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He regrets not having taken with the Messenger the path to Paradise through Islam.
rows.anchor: ندماً وتحسراً { يقول يا ليتني اتخذت مع الرسول سبيلا } طريقا إلى الجنة بالإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The friend he regrets choosing is Ubayy ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: فلانا } يعني: أبيا { خليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is the Qur'an; Ubayy misled him away from it after it came, and Satan abandons a person in adversity. Accepting Ubayy's call to disbelief was the work of Satan.
rows.anchor: القرآن { بعد إذ جاءني وكان الشيطان للإنسان خذولا } عند البلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day the Messenger complains that his people abandoned the Qur'an and turned away from it.
rows.anchor: في ذلك اليوم: يا { رب إن قومي اتخذوا هذا القرآن مهجورا } متروكا أعرضوا عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God appointed criminals as enemies to every prophet and is sufficient to guide and help Muhammad, so he should not worry about his enemies.
rows.anchor: وكما جعلنا لك أعداء من المشركين { جعلنا لكل نبي عدوا من المجرمين

words: لَوْلَا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْقُرْءَانُ جُمْلَةً وَٰحِدَةً
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers objected that the Qur'an was revealed in portions instead of all at once, as they said the Torah and Gospel were.
rows.anchor: أي: لم نزل عليه متفرقا؟ وهلا كان دفعة واحدة كالتوراة والإنجيل؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its gradual revelation strengthened the Prophet's heart as each new revelation came; God made its delivery clear, measured, and unhurried.
rows.anchor: لنقوي به قلبك، وذلك أنه كلما نزل عليه وحي جديد ازداد هو قوة قلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an was made clear through steady, measured delivery.
rows.anchor: ورتلناه ترتيلا } بيناه تبيينا في تثبت ومهلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of Muhammad is found in the books of earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: ذكر محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { لفي زبر الأولين } لفي كتب الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the polytheists, a sign of Muhammad's truth is that the scholars of the Children of Israel know him as prophet and messenger.
rows.anchor: دلالة على صدقه { أن يعلمه علماء بني إسرائيل } يعلمون محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم بالنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is explained as “so that they do not prostrate to God.”
rows.anchor: ألا يسجدوا } أي: لأن لا يسجدوا لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God brings forth from concealment is rain from the sky and vegetation from the earth.
rows.anchor: القطر من السماء، والنبات من الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawajjaha means that Moses set out toward Midian.
rows.anchor: قصد بوجهه { تلقاء مدين } نحوها { قال عسى ربي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked God to guide him to the right road because he did not know the route.
rows.anchor: قصد الطريق، وذلك أنه لم يكن يعرف الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water of Midian was their well, where a group of people watered their livestock.
rows.anchor: وهو بئر لهم { وجد عليه أمة } جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two women held their sheep back from the water until the shepherds finished, since they could not draw water while competing with the men; their father was too old to do it.
rows.anchor: لأنا لا نطيق أن نستقي وأن نزاحم الرجال، فإذا صدروا سقينا من فضل مواشيهم { وأبونا شيخ كبير } لا يمكنه أن يرد وأن يستقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses watered their sheep from another well by lifting a rock that normally took ten men to lift.
rows.anchor: أغنامهما من بئر أخرى رفع عنها حجرا كان لا يرفعه إلا عشرة أنفس

words: إِنِّى لِمَآ أَنزَلْتَ إِلَىَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses went to the shade of a tree and asked God for food because he was hungry; after hearing what Moses had done, the women told their father, who sent one of them to invite him.
rows.anchor: وكان قد جاع فسأل الله تعالى ما يأكل، فلما رجعتا إلى أبيهما أخبرتاه بما فعل موسى، فقال لإحداهما

rows.speaker: إحداهما
rows.claim: One daughter recommended hiring Moses to tend their sheep, judging him the best hire because he was strong and trustworthy.
rows.anchor: قالت إحداهما يا أبت استأجره } ليرعى أغنامنا { إن خير من استأجرت القوي الأمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She knew his strength from his lifting the well's rock and his trustworthiness from his instruction that she walk behind him, since the descendants of Jacob do not look at women's backs.
rows.anchor: عرفت قوته برفع الحجر من رأس البئر، وأمانته بأن موسى قال لها لما دعته إلى أبيها

rows.speaker: الشيخ
rows.claim: The old man offered Moses marriage to one of his two daughters in exchange for eight years of service; completing ten would be voluntary, and he did not wish to burden Moses but promised to keep the agreement.
rows.anchor: عند ذلك الشيخ لموسى: { إني أريد أن أنكحك } أزوجك { إحدى ابنتي هاتين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra two years were not an obligation; the father said he would not impose that burden and would be faithful to the covenant.
rows.anchor: وليس بواجب عليك { وما أريد أن أشق عليك } بأن اشترط العشر { ستجدني إن شاء الله من الصالحين } الوافين بالعهد

words: أَيَّمَا ٱلْأَجَلَيْنِ قَضَيْتُ فَلَا عُدْوَٰنَ عَلَىَّ
rows.speaker: موسى
rows.claim: Moses accepted the described terms: the father would give a daughter in marriage and Moses would serve for the agreed period; he could not be unjustly required to serve longer than either term he completed.
rows.anchor: ذلك } الذي وصفت { بيني وبينك } أي: لك ما شرطت علي ولي ما شرطت من تزويج إحداهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is witness to the agreement they made.
rows.anchor: والله على ما نقول وكيل } والله شاهدنا على ما عقدنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asked who sends rain and revives the earth, the polytheists answer “God”; Muhammad is to praise God for sending rain to revive the earth.
rows.anchor: ليقولن الله قل الحمد لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most lack the understanding by which they could recognize truth and falsehood.
rows.anchor: العقل الذي يعرفون به الحق من الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This worldly life is diversion and play because it soon passes away, while the hereafter is lasting life; they fail to know that permanence.
rows.anchor: لنفادها عن قريب { وإن الدار الآخرة لهي الحيوان } الحياة الدائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When fearing drowning at sea, they call on God sincerely; once He saves them on land, they return to associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: دعوا الله مخلصين له الدين فلما نجاهم إلى البر إذا هم يشركون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is apparently an imperative of threat: they are commanded to deny God's gift of rescue, as the following threat confirms.
rows.anchor: أي: ليجحدوا بما أنعمنا عليهم من إنجائهم، والظاهر أن هذ لام الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans have a secure sanctuary where its people are not attacked, while people around them are seized by killing, robbery, and captivity.
rows.anchor: يعني: أهل مكة { أنا جعلنا حرما آمنا } ذا أمن لا يغار على أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The falsehood they believe is idols; the favor of God they reject is Muhammad and the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: يعني: الأصنام { وبنعمة الله } يعني: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم والقرآن

words: مِّن رِّبًا لِّيَرْبُوَا فِىٓ أَمْوَٰلِ ٱلنَّاسِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The riba described is a permissible gift given in expectation of receiving more back; it does not grow with God because the giver did not seek God's pleasure.
rows.anchor: يعني: ما يعطونه من الهدية ليأخذوا أكثر منها، وهو من الربا الحلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The multipliers are those whose reward is increased tenfold for each unit given.
rows.anchor: أصحاب الإضعاف، يضاعف لهم بالواحدة عشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barren land is hard, with no vegetation.
rows.anchor: الغليظة التي لا نبات فيها { فنخرج به زرعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending water that produces crops for people and livestock is evidence that God can resurrect the dead.
rows.anchor: هذا فيعلموا أنا نقدر على إعادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wherever people are, they see sky and land before and behind them and cannot escape them; they should not feel secure from God's power.
rows.anchor: أما يعلمون أنهم حيث ما كانوا فهم يرون ما بين أيديهم من الأرض والسماء مثل الذي خلفهم

words: نَخْسِفْ بِهِمُ ٱلْأَرْضَ أَوْ نُسْقِطْ عَلَيْهِمْ كِسَفًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God could punish them by making the earth swallow them or dropping fragments from the sky.
rows.anchor: إن نشأ نخسف بهم الأرض أو نسقط عليهم كسفا من السماء } عذابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For anyone who turns back to God and reflects on creation, this is a sign of God's ability to raise the dead.
rows.anchor: لآية لكل عبد منيب } لعلامة تدل على قدرة الله سبحانه على إحياء الموتى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told the mountains to glorify with David; when he glorified, they answered, and birds gathered above him to join in the praise.
rows.anchor: أي: قلنا يا جبال { أوبي معه } سبحي معه { والطير } كان إذا سبح جاوبته الجبال بالتسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made iron soft in David's hand like wet clay or dough.
rows.anchor: جعلناه لينا في يده، كالطين المبلول والعجين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sābighāt are complete coats of mail.
rows.anchor: دروعا كوامل { وقدر في السرد } لا تجعل مسمار الدرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sard is the weaving of chain mail; each rivet should be sized so it neither splits when too thin nor breaks the rings when too thick.
rows.anchor: لا تجعل مسمار الدرع دقيقا فيفلق، ولا غليظا فيفصم الحلق. اجعله على قدر الحاجة، والسرد: نسج الدروع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to do good is addressed to David and his family and means doing righteous acts in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: يعني: داود وآله { صالحا } عملا صالحا من طاعة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Solomon's wind traveled a month's journey between morning and noon and another month's journey between noon and night.
rows.anchor: مسيرها إلى انتصاف النهار مسيرة شهر، ومن انتصاف النهار إلى الليل مسيرة شهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God melted a spring of copper for Solomon, and it flowed like water.
rows.anchor: أذبنا له عين النحاس، فسالت له كما يسيل الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God subjected jinn to work for Solomon by the Lord's command; they were charged to obey Solomon.
rows.anchor: أي: سخرنا له من الجن { من يعمل بين يديه بإذن ربه } بأمر ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A jinn who deviated from the command to obey Solomon faced blazing punishment; God assigned an angel with a fiery whip that burned any offender with one strike.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن الله تعالى وكل بهم ملكا بيده سوط من نار، فمن زاغ عن أمر سليمان ضربه ضربة أحرقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul bearing sin carries another soul's sin.
rows.anchor: لا تحمل نفس حاملة { وزر أخرى } حمل نفس أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if a sin-laden person calls a close relative such as a father or son to carry the burden, none of it will be taken from that person.
rows.anchor: نفس مثقلة بالذنوب { إلى حملها } ذنوبها { لا يحمل منه شيء ولو كان } المدعو { ذا قربى } مثل الأب والابن

words: إِنَّمَا تُنذِرُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلْغَيْبِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning benefits those who fear God without having seen Him.
rows.anchor: إنما ينفع إنذارك الذين يخافون الله تعالى، ولم يروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who purifies himself does good.
rows.anchor: لم يروه { ومن تزكى } عمل خيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blind person is the unbeliever who misses truth; the sighted person is the believer who sees the right path.
rows.anchor: عن الحق، وهو الكافر { والبصير } الذي يبصر رشده، وهو المؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darknesses stand for unbelief and light for faith.
rows.anchor: ولا الظلمات ولا النور } يعني: الكفر والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shade is Paradise's lasting shade, while ḥarūr is the fire's intense heat.
rows.anchor: يعني: الجنة التي فيها ظل دائم، والنار التي لها حرارة شديدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living are believers and the dead are unbelievers; God enables whom He wills to hear and benefit.
rows.anchor: يعني: المؤمنين والكفار { إن الله يسمع من يشاء } فينتفع بذلك

words: وَمَآ أَنتَ بِمُسْمِعٍ مَّن فِى ٱلْقُبُورِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people in graves are unbelievers compared to the dead: just as grave-dwellers do not hear, unbelievers do not hear the message.
rows.anchor: يعني: الكفار، شبههم بالأموات، أي: كما لا يسمع أصحاب القبور كذلك لا يسمع الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white and red judad are streaks running through mountains like veins.
rows.anchor: أي: طرائق تكون في الجبال كالعروق بيض وحمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gharābīb refers to mountains with black rocks.
rows.anchor: وهي الجبال ذات الصخور السود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans, animals, and livestock vary in color just as mountains and fruits do.
rows.anchor: أي: كاختلاف الجبال والثمرات في اختلاف الألوان

words: إِنَّمَا يَخْشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنْ عِبَادِهِ ٱلْعُلَمَٰٓؤُا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who know God are the ones who fear Him intensely.
rows.anchor: من كان عالما بالله اشتدت خشيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised trade will neither languish nor fail.
rows.anchor: يعني: لن تكسد ولن تفسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives their sins and rewards their good deeds appreciatively.
rows.anchor: إنه غفور } لذنوبهم { شكور } لحسناتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After earlier nations perished, God gave the Qur'an to Muhammad's community as a great favor.
rows.anchor: أعطينا بعد هلاك الأمم { الكتاب } القرآن ل { الذين اصطفينا من عبادنا } وهم أمة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three groups are the wrongdoer, whose sins outweigh good deeds; the moderate, whose good and bad deeds are equal; and the foremost, whose good deeds outweigh sins.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي زادت سيئاته على حسناته { ومنهم مقتصد } وهو الذي استوت حسناته وسيئاته { ومنهم سابق بالخيرات } وهو الذي رجحت حسناته

words: بِإِذْنِ ٱللَّهِ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلْفَضْلُ ٱلْكَبِيرُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The positions among the three groups are by God's decree and will.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي رجحت حسناته { بإذن الله } بقضائه وإرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People did not make these fruits and have no part in producing them.
rows.anchor: أي: لم تعمله ولا صنع لهم في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pairs God created include the kinds of plants and animals.
rows.anchor: أي: الأجناس من النبات والحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God also created every other kind and likeness unknown to people.
rows.anchor: مما خلق الله سبحانه من جميع الأنواع والأشباه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of night is a sign for people of God's oneness and power.
rows.anchor: ودلالة لهم على توحيد الله سبحانه وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God strips away the daylight completely and brings night, leaving people in darkness.
rows.anchor: إخراجا لا يبقى معه شيء من ضوء النهار، والمعنى: ننزع النهار فنذهب به، ونأتي بالليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun runs to its appointed setting at the end of the world.
rows.anchor: أي: وآية لهم الشمس { تجري لمستقر لها } عند انقضاء الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At its last phase the moon resembles an old, dried, curved date-cluster stalk.
rows.anchor: ذا منازل { حتى عاد } في آخر منزله { كالعرجون القديم } وهو عود الشمراخ إذا يبس اعوج

words: لَا ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنبَغِى لَهَآ أَن تُدْرِكَ ٱلْقَمَرَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun does not catch up with the moon so that the two join together.
rows.anchor: الشمس ينبغي لها أن تدرك القمر } فيجتمعا معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night does not overtake day by arriving before day has ended.
rows.anchor: ولا الليل سابق النهار } يسبقه فيأتي قبل انقضاء النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun, moon, and stars all travel in an orbit.
rows.anchor: من الشمس والقمر والنجوم { في فلك يسبحون }. [يسيرون]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abaqa means Jonah fled; he had left in anger and boarded a full ship.
rows.anchor: إذ أبق } هرب { إلى الفلك المشحون } السفينة المملوءة حين ذهب مغاضبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship stopped moving, so its passengers cast lots; Jonah lost, went out of the ship, and threw himself into the sea.
rows.anchor: فقارعه أهل السفينة فخرجت القرعة عليه، فخرج منها وألقى نفسه في البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāhama means to draw lots, and Jonah was among those defeated by the lot.
rows.anchor: فقارع { فكان من المدحضين } المغلوبين بالقرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fish swallowed Jonah, who had done something for which he could be blamed.
rows.anchor: فابتلعه { الحوت وهم مليم } أتى بما يلام عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah had been among those who prayed before this event.
rows.anchor: فلولا أنه كان من المسبحين } من المصلين قبل ذلك

words: لَلَبِثَ فِى بَطْنِهِۦٓ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without his prior worship, Jonah would have remained in the fish's belly until the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: في بطن الحوت إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cast Jonah onto open ground while he was ill, like a newly hatched, featherless chick.
rows.anchor: طرحناه { بالعراء } وجه الأرض { وهو سقيم } عليل كالفرخ الممعط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grew a gourd plant beside Jonah so he could take shade beneath it.
rows.anchor: عنده { شجرة من يقطين } وهو القرع ليستظل بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people to whom Jonah was sent numbered more than one hundred thousand.
rows.anchor: وأرسلناه إلى مائة ألف أو يزيدون } بل يزيدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They believed, and God let them enjoy life until their appointed terms ended.
rows.anchor: فآمنوا فمتعناهم إلى حين } إلى انقضاء آجالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God takes souls at death and also takes the souls of those who have not died during sleep; He keeps the dead and returns the others when they wake, until their appointed time of death.
rows.anchor: يقْبض الأرواح { حين } عند { موتها والتي لم تمت } أي: ويقبض روح التي لم تمت

words: أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ شُفَعَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supposed intercessors worshipped besides God are the idols.
rows.anchor: أي: الأوثان التي عبدوها لتشفع لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols possess no power of intercession and do not understand the worship directed to them.
rows.anchor: من الشفاعة { ولا يعقلون } أنهم يعبدونهم لا يتركون عبادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All intercession belongs to God; no one intercedes without His permission.
rows.anchor: فليس يشفع أحد إلا بإذنه

words: ٱشْمَأَزَّتْ قُلُوبُ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلْءَاخِرَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists recoiled when they heard God named alone but rejoiced when idols were mentioned; ishmaʾazzat means recoiled.
rows.anchor: كان المشركون إذا سمعوا قول لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له نفروا من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who went to excess against themselves committed major sins and shameful acts.
rows.anchor: بارتكاب الكبائر والفواحش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Meccans intended to embrace Islam but feared their past idolatry, associating partners, and killing could not be forgiven; God revealed that whoever repents and believes can be forgiven every sin.
rows.anchor: نزلت في قوم من أهل مكة هموا بالإسلام، ثم قالوا:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To turn back is to return to obedience, and to submit to God is to obey Him.
rows.anchor: أي: ارجعوا إليه الطاعة { وأسلموا } وأطيعوا { له }

words: أَحْسَنَ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best thing sent down is the Qur'an, as also stated in 39:23.
rows.anchor: أي: القرآن، كقوله: { الله نزل أحسن الحديث }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should turn back and follow the Qur'an before sudden punishment arrives, so they do not face the coming regret.
rows.anchor: افعلوا ما أمرتكم به من الإنابة واتباع القرآن خوف أن تصيروا إلى حالة تقولون فيها هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regret is for having neglected obedience to God and following His way.
rows.anchor: أي: قصرت في طاعة الله، وسلوك طريقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker admits to having mocked God's religion and Book.
rows.anchor: ما كنت إلا من المستهزئين بدين الله تعالى وكتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to call on God means to worship Him, for which He will reward and forgive them.
rows.anchor: ادعوني أستجب لكم } اعبدوني أثبكم وأغفر لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dākhirīn means humbled and abased.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { داخرين } أي: صاغرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is barren and dusty, with no plants.
rows.anchor: مغبرة لا نبات فيها { فإذا أنزلنا عليهم الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth moves with vegetation, swells and rises, then splits open to produce plants.
rows.anchor: تحركت بالنبات { وربت } انتفخت وعلت، ثم تصدعت عن النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who deviate regarding God's signs twist their meaning and accuse them of being lies and sorcery.
rows.anchor: يجعلون الكلام فيها على غير جهته، بأن ينسبوها إلى الكذب والسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are not hidden from God: He knows them and will requite them.
rows.anchor: بل نعلمهم ونجازيهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reminder is the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: أي: بالقرآن { لما جاءهم وإنه لكتاب عزيز } منيع من الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is protected and invulnerable to Satan and falsehood.
rows.anchor: وإنه لكتاب عزيز } منيع من الشيطان والباطل

words: لَا يَأْتِيهِ ٱلْبَٰطِلُ مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier books cannot invalidate the Qur'an, and no later book will invalidate it.
rows.anchor: الكتب التي تقدمت لا تبطله، ولا يأتي كتاب بعده يبطله

words: مِن بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative explanation says the Qur'an is protected from being diminished or having additions inserted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه محفوظ من أن ينقص منه فيأتيه الباطل من بين يديه، أو يزاد فيه فيأتيه الباطل من خلفه

words: مَا يُقَالُ لَكَ إِلَّا مَا قَدْ قِيلَ لِلرُّسُلِ مِن قَبْلِكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's people have called him a liar just as earlier peoples called their messengers liars.
rows.anchor: أي: إن كذبك قومك فقد كذب الذين من قبلك
